tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Current project, plan, credits and limits, warm-up status, verified sending domains and whether this connection uses a test key. Call this first.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Projects (workspaces) the signed-in user belongs to.

tools.name: switch_project
tools.description: Point this AI connection at another of the user's projects. Only for OAuth connections; API keys always belong to one project.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send one transactional email (sign-in link, receipt, notification). Use html and/or text, or a saved template with data. With a live key this delivers a real email, so it asks for confirmation. With a test key nothing is delivered.
tools.level: Asks you first with a live key; runs directly with a test key

tools.name: get_email
tools.description: Status and content of one transactional email: queued, sent, delivered, bounced, complained, opened, clicked, or test.

tools.name: list_deliveries
tools.description: Recent emails across transactional and broadcasts with their delivery status. Use it to answer why an email bounced or did not arrive.

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: Sending domains and their verification status.

tools.name: add_domain
tools.description: Add a domain to send from. Returns the DNS records (DKIM CNAMEs, SPF, DMARC) the user must add at their DNS provider. Then use check_domain.

tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Re-check a domain's verification and DNS records, with exactly which record is missing.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Saved email templates with their variables.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: One template with its HTML, text and variables.

tools.name: save_template
tools.description: Create a template, or update the one with the same name. Use {{variable}} for escaped values and {{{variable}}} for raw HTML. kind is transactional (always delivered) or marketing (skipped for unsubscribed contacts).

tools.name: delete_template
tools.description: Delete a template. Emails or workflows using it will fail, so this asks for confirmation.

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description: Contacts in the project.

tools.name: upsert_contact
tools.description: Create a contact or update their name, custom data and tags. Records a contact.saved event.

tools.name: track_event
tools.description: Record that a contact did something (user.signed_up, order.paid). Creates the contact if needed and starts any workflow triggered by this event, which may send emails.

tools.name: list_segments
tools.description: Saved audiences built from rules, with their size.

tools.name: create_segment
tools.description: Save an audience from rules. Each rule is {"field","op","value"}; fields include email, first_name, last_name, status, tag, created_at, last_engaged_at, event, data.<field>. Use {"field":"group","op":"any"/"all","rules":[...]} for one nested group. Call call_api with POST /api/segments/preview to check the size first.

tools.name: create_broadcast
tools.description: Create a newsletter or announcement as a draft. Nothing is sent until the user confirms send_broadcast in the chat.

tools.name: send_broadcast
tools.description: Launch a broadcast draft to its whole audience. It can't be undone, so the user must confirm it in the chat first.

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: Sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced and complaint numbers with rates, compared with the previous period.

tools.name: create_api_key
tools.description: Create an API key for the user's app. mode test (default) stores emails without delivering them; mode live sends for real. The key is shown once: tell the user to put it in an environment variable (FORKE_MAIL_API_KEY), never in code.

tools.name: call_api
tools.description: Call any /api endpoint for things the other tools do not cover (workflows, topics, suppressions, team, webhooks, settings, campaigns, reports). Reading is free; risky changes ask the user to confirm in the chat. See the resource forke-mail://guide for the endpoint list.
tools.level: Depends on the endpoint (see Safety model)

prompts.title: Set up Forke Mail in my app
prompts.description: Add email to the project you're working on: key, helper, first test send.
prompts.text:
Set up Forke Mail in this web project.
1. Call get_account to check my project, verified domains and limits.
2. Create a test key with create_api_key (mode "test"), add it to .env as FORKE_MAIL_API_KEY, and make sure .env is in .gitignore.
3. Add a sendEmail helper that calls POST https://mail.forke.space/api/transactional with the key from the environment and an Idempotency-Key header.
4. Send one test email through the helper and show me the result.
5. Tell me what I need to switch to live sending (a verified domain and a live key).
prompts.name: setup-app

prompts.title: Create a welcome email
prompts.description: Design a welcome email template that matches your product.
prompts.text:
Create a welcome email template for my product with a friendly tone.
Use save_template named "welcome" (kind transactional) with {{name}} for the person's name and a clear call to action button. Keep the HTML simple and mobile friendly, and include a plain-text version. Then send me a preview with a test key.
prompts.name: welcome-email

prompts.title: Add sign-in and password reset emails
prompts.description: Templates and code for magic links, one-time codes and password resets.
prompts.text:
Add sign-in and password reset emails to this web app with Forke Mail.
Create templates "sign-in-code" ({{code}}, expires in 10 minutes) and "password-reset" ({{reset_link}}) with save_template, then wire them into the existing auth flow using the template name and data. Use an Idempotency-Key per request so retries never send twice.
prompts.name: auth-emails

prompts.title: Build a welcome email series
prompts.description: A workflow that sends a short series after someone signs up.
prompts.text:
Build a welcome series that starts when the user.signed_up event is tracked.
Draft three short emails (day 0, day 2, day 5) as templates, then create a workflow with call_api POST /api/workflows using wait and send steps, exiting if the person does the main action. Show me the plan before you create the workflow, and track one test event to check it.
prompts.name: welcome-series

prompts.title: Write and send a newsletter
prompts.description: Draft a broadcast for a segment and send it when you're happy.
prompts.text:
Write a newsletter about our latest update for the main segment.
Check the segment size with list_segments, draft it with create_broadcast (keep the {{unsubscribe_url}} link), show me the subject and content, and only call send_broadcast after I say yes.
prompts.name: newsletter

prompts.title: Verify my sending domain
prompts.description: Add a domain and walk through the DNS records step by step.
prompts.text:
Help me send email from my domain.
Add it with add_domain, then show me each DNS record as a small table (type, name, value) for my DNS provider. After I add them, run check_domain and tell me exactly which record is still missing until it's verified.
prompts.name: verify-domain

prompts.title: Why didn't my email arrive?
prompts.description: Find a missing email and explain what happened.
prompts.text: An email to the recipient didn't arrive. Use list_deliveries with that address, then get_email for the latest one, and explain in plain words what happened (sent, delivered, bounced, suppressed or failed) and what I should do next.
prompts.name: debug-delivery

prompts.title: Move to Forke Mail from another provider
prompts.description: Replace Resend, SendGrid, Postmark or SES calls in your code.
prompts.text:
Move this codebase from my current provider to Forke Mail.
Find every place that sends email, list them for me first, then replace them with calls to POST https://mail.forke.space/api/transactional (or templates where the same email repeats). Keep the same from addresses, add idempotency keys, and use a test key until I say to go live.
prompts.name: migrate

prompts.title: How are my emails doing?
prompts.description: A short report on delivery, opens, clicks and problems.
prompts.text: Give me a short report on my email over the last 7 days using get_analytics and list_deliveries with status "problems": what was sent, delivery and open rates compared with the week before, and anything that bounced or was reported as spam, with one suggestion to improve.
prompts.name: weekly-report
